name: Magellan
first: Most complete radar map of Venus — 98% of the surface at ~120-m resolution; first planetary spacecraft launched from the Space Shuttle
description: Magellan turned Venus from a featureless cloud-veiled disc into a mapped planet. Launched from Shuttle Atlantis's payload bay 1989-05-04 — the first planetary spacecraft to ride a Shuttle — and arrived at Venus 1990-08-10 via a long Type-IV trajectory (1.5 solar revolutions). Over four mapping cycles the synthetic-aperture radar imaged 98% of Venus's surface at ~120-m resolution, revealing tessera highlands, coronae, pancake domes, and a young, volcanically-resurfaced surface. Mission ended 1994-10-13 in the Termination Experiment — the first planned controlled atmospheric entry of a planetary spacecraft.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: STS-30 / Atlantis from Kennedy LC-39B; IUS deployed from Shuttle bay.

events.label: VOI
events.note: Solid-motor burn into a 295 × 8543 km, 85.5° near-polar orbit.

events.label: MAPPING CYCLE 1 COMPLETE
events.note: First full pass — 84% surface coverage at 100 m resolution.

events.label: TERMINATION EXPERIMENT
events.note: 1994-10-13. Periapsis lowered into atmosphere — first planned planetary spacecraft entry.
